blockers_and_notes: store.ts and engine.ts had NO couple support at task start (no registerCouple/getCoupleForUser/getGroupCoupleMode/setGroupCoupleMode/getCouplesInGroup/removeCouple, no CoupleNettingConfig/netCoupleBalances). A concurrent sibling subagent (sa-0-99cb66ed) is implementing those layers. I did NOT implement them (out of scope and would collide), but I DID need to revert an accidental engine.ts edit that created a duplicate CoupleNettingConfig interface.

api.ts had scope overlap with the sibling: it had already added netCoupleBalances import and a getSuggestedSettlements(groupId, netting?) version. I reconciled by keeping the optional netting override AND defaulting the config from the store (so plain getSuggestedSettlements(groupId) works, as the UI calls it), and restored the netCoupleBalances import that my earlier import edit had dropped.

Cross-device couple identity (AC 7): the sibling's store.registerCouple mints a fresh uuid per device and does not accept a uuid; store.removeCouple is idempotent by device-local numeric id. So couple registration/unregistration syncs the relationship but does not preserve a shared uuid across devices — a store-layer design limitation outside my three files.

Schema version: the task said 'bump from 3 to 4' but the actual CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION was 1. I bumped 1 → 2 (the correct increment against the real value) and migrate from any version < CURRENT. Jumping to 4 would have rejected every existing v1 export.

Since the sibling is actively editing store.ts/engine.ts/api.ts, the build is only guaranteed clean at the moment I verified it (EXIT=0). Further concurrent edits by the sibling may transiently re-break it; my code targets the contract the sibling has already landed.
